mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-01.title: Count bags, then boxes
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-01.body:
Bags needed: $7 \times 14 = 98$. Boxes: $98 \div 10 = 9.8$, so 9 boxes (90 bags) are not enough; he must buy **10** boxes.

**Answer: 10 boxes**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-01.title: Check 9 vs 10 boxes
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-01.body:
9 boxes hold 90 bags, which covers only $90 \div 7 \approx 12.9$ yards — fewer than 14. 10 boxes hold 100 bags, enough for $14 \times 7 = 98$.

**Answer: 10 boxes**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-02.title: Count the steps
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-02.body:
The temperature drops 3 degrees every 5 days. From 60° (October 31) to 33° is a drop of $27$ degrees, i.e. $27 \div 3 = 9$ steps, which is $9 \times 5 = 45$ days after October 31.

November has 30 days, so 30 days after October 31 is November 30, and 15 more days is **December 15**.

**Answer: December 15**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-02.title: List the sequence
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-02.body:
Oct 31: 60, Nov 5: 57, Nov 10: 54, Nov 15: 51, Nov 20: 48, Nov 25: 45, Nov 30: 42, Dec 5: 39, Dec 10: 36, Dec 15: 33.

**Answer: December 15**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-03.title: List the skipped days
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-03.body:
Lou skips exactly 3 of the 7 days, and no two skipped days may be next to each other. Write the days as S, M, T, W, R, F, Q (Sunday … Saturday) and list the skipped triples:

- Starting with S: (S,T,R), (S,T,F), (S,T,Q), (S,W,F), (S,W,Q), (S,R,Q) — 6
- Starting with M: (M,W,F), (M,W,Q), (M,R,Q) — 3
- Starting with T: (T,R,Q) — 1

Total: $6 + 3 + 1 = 10$.

**Answer: 10**

mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-03.title: Gaps between workout days
mathcounts-potw-2025-11-17-03.body:
Line up the 4 workout days: X X X X. They create 5 gaps (before, between, after). Each skipped day goes into a different gap so that no two skipped days touch. Choosing 3 of the 5 gaps: $\binom{5}{3} = 10$.

**Answer: 10**
